newsitem.title: USA: Florida court clears Tampa Sports Authority deal.
newsitem.headline: Florida court clears Tampa Sports Authority deal.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court has refused without comment to reconsider its validation of the revenue bonds that will finance the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' new stadium, a court clerk said Thursday.
The decision late Wednesday clears the way for the Tampa Sports Authority's $190 million bond issue, which has been on the day-to-day calender at Smith Barney Inc pending the ruling.
Construction on the 65,000-seat stadium began last fall, shortly after voters approved a sales tax increase for the stadium and other projects.

But the bond issue was delayed when former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe filed suit arguing that the stadium plan was unconstitutional because it would use public funds to benefit the private, for-profit football team.
Hillsborough County Circuit Judge Sam Pendino ruled in Poe's favor but said he would validate the bonds if certain changes were made in the contract with the team.

Poe appealed to the state Supreme Court, which unanimously rejected Poe's argument and validated the bonds on May 22. Poe sought a rehearing, and the seven-member court unanimously rejected the request on Wednesday.
Without the bond proceeds, the city and county would have had only enough money to continue construction through July 1.
